extracted.intended_audience: State apprenticeship agencies (SAAs), State government agencies seeking recognition from the Office of Apprenticeship (OA), State workforce and education policymakers, and stakeholders preparing comments
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for State Apprenticeship Plans and SAA recognition, including submission cadence, required plan contents (strategic, operational, and assurances), recognition designations (full/provisional/denial), reporting/data requirements, and monitoring/remedy procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: State planning cycle and submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: State Apprenticeship Plans are due every 4 years (departing from current 5-year cycle); SAAs seeking recognition must submit plans at least 120 days prior to proposed effective date. First planning cycle special timing: first cycle covers Jan 1, 2027–June 30, 2030; second cycle begins July 1, 2030. A State may seek recognition at any time but must align its approved SAA plan with the next State apprenticeship planning cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change to 4-year cycle aimed to align apprenticeship planning with WIOA/Perkins state planning; selection of Dec 31, 2026 as a reference provides ~2 years transition time. Department requests comments on ability to transition and potential flexibilities; examples given for alignment and transitional scenarios (e.g., receiving recognition in July 2028 still requires submission for July 1, 2030 cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: State law standard — meet or exceed minimum Federal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A State's apprenticeship laws must meet or exceed the minimum requirements set forth in 29 CFR parts 29 and 30 for protecting the safety and welfare of apprentices (replacing the prior 'conformity' standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides States flexibility to innovate beyond mirroring part 29 so long as the deviations advance apprentice safety/welfare (examples: higher/more frequent wage progressions, more frequent program reviews, more instructor training, additional protections). The Department seeks comments on applying this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core registration requirements to be included in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State must submit proposed or current apprenticeship laws governing: standards of apprenticeship; apprenticeship agreements; registration requirements; program standards adoption agreements; qualifications of apprentice trainers and providers of related instruction; end-point assessments; complaints; recordkeeping; processes for program review and deregistration; roles and responsibilities of SAAs; and reporting requirements for an SAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are deemed core requirements of Registration Agencies and form the baseline by which OA assesses that a State meets minimum quality requirements for registration functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with education and workforce systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The SAA must coordinate with the State's education system (including institutions of higher education, LEAs, State CTE and Educational Agencies, and other educational entities supporting CTE and career pathways) and describe efforts to align and leverage apprenticeship-related data with education and workforce development system data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination is intended to strengthen alignment with CTE, WIOA, Perkins and to enable shared planning and data-driven strategies across systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning elements
rubrics_metrics.description: State Apprenticeship Plans must include strategic planning elements: a vision for expanding/improving registered apprenticeship; goals for expanding the model; goals for promoting apprenticeship for underserved communities; goals for aligning apprenticeship with broader education and workforce activities; activities to coordinate with economic development entities; and strategies to engage and leverage industry intermediaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic elements should use individual and cross-sectional labor market data (past, present, future) to justify strategies. OA uses these elements to assess alignment with federal goals for modernization, expansion, and equity. Examples and rationale link to ACA recommendations and system alignment objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational planning elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational elements required in an initial plan include: State's EEO plan (in conformity with part 30); technical assistance plan; process to meet performance reporting requirements (including use of data management tools/procedures); plan for conducting program reviews; plans to operationalize registration standards; reciprocity policy (per proposed §29.26(f)); and the structure of the State Apprenticeship Council consistent with §29.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational elements describe how the State will implement the strategic vision and perform SAA roles. They are required for recognition and are evaluated for completeness and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances to be provided
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must provide specific assurances: that the State will provide a process for local registration of National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards; that the State has resources necessary to operate the SAA and can carry out SAA responsibilities; that the State will maintain a publicly available website describing apprenticeship-related laws/regulations/policies/procedures; and that the State will require sponsors' written assurance of compliance with the Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act of 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurances are intended as a streamlined method to confirm key operational commitments; the Department requests comments on their sufficiency and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship registration pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State seeks recognition to register CTE apprenticeship programs under subpart B, the State must submit proposed/current CTE apprenticeship laws as part of the plan, include the written agreement between the Registration Agency (per §29.24(a)(2)), and provide a narrative describing how it will develop and expand registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTE recognition is optional and distinct from subpart A recognition; this requirement ensures strategic alignment for both subpart A and subpart B activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for full recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: For OA to convey full recognition, the State Apprenticeship Plan must demonstrate: minimum labor standards; a comprehensive plan addressing strategic and operational elements necessary to expand quality registered apprenticeship programs; clear commitments and progress on promoting equity; and strategies integrating workforce development and educational activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions are necessary to ensure the State can fulfill the increased role OA envisions for SAAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and nature of provisional recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional recognition is conveyed when a State provides a minimally sufficient plan that meets minimum requirements but has one or more deficiencies (e.g., incomplete strategic/operational elements such as lacking a technical assistance strategy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA will require submission and approval of a corrective action plan detailing actionable steps and timelines to address deficiencies. A State may not remain provisionally recognized for more than one full planning cycle. OA will provide technical assistance during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial is appropriate when the Administrator determines the State's apprenticeship laws do not meet the minimum standards in §29.27(b)(1) or when an SAA cannot be fully approved after being provisionally recognized for one full planning cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial procedures and appeals are described in proposed §29.29; the Department explains the processes and consequences in that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification triggers and process for State Apprenticeship Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs must modify their State Apprenticeship Plan when changes in Federal or State law, labor market conditions, State vision/strategies/policies/operations/organizational structure materially impact the ability to fulfill the approved plan. SAAs may also elect discretionary modifications (e.g., changing recognition status or seeking CTE recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications must be submitted at least 120 days prior to the requested effective date. If approved, modifications remain in effect until the end of the original plan cycle. OA will determine whether modified submissions meet approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reviews, and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: OA will monitor and review SAAs to ensure operations are consistent with approved State Apprenticeship Plans. Although the plan cycle provides a regular 4-year review cadence, OA may schedule more frequent reviews in certain instances (e.g., to review corrective action plan progress for provisionally recognized states).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department seeks comments on when periodic reviews should occur outside the 4-year cycle; reviews can be used to provide technical assistance or conclude that revision is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension of authority to register new programs
rubrics_metrics.description: OA may suspend an SAA's authority to register new apprenticeship programs where a corrective action plan is not submitted for review and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension process: OA provides written notice; suspension becomes effective 30 calendar days after the written notice and ends upon the State's submission of an acceptable corrective action plan. Suspension is envisioned as an interim accountability step prior to derecognition; OA solicits comments on other interim options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derecognition consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State Apprenticeship Plan is denied or the Administrator derecognizes an SAA, the State government agency may not function as an SAA for Federal purposes (i.e., cannot conduct operations enumerated in proposed §29.26(a)) until OA conveys full or provisional recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that have been denied or derecognized may submit an updated or new State Apprenticeship Plan to pursue recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial/derecognition notice and remedial timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: When OA denies a plan or derecognizes an SAA, a written notice must explain the reasons and identify remedial measures and set a timeline (no longer than 12 months after the notice date) for addressing those measures. Failure to remedy within the timeframe may lead to a final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 12 months is chosen to allow States time (including legislative session scheduling) to make necessary legal changes while preventing an open-ended timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required apprentice and sponsor data reporting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs must collect and report individual apprentice records at least quarterly and sponsor records at least annually to the Department (as defined in proposed §29.25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting may be done via Department-provided case management systems (e.g., RAPIDS) or through interoperable state systems that report accurate, timely data in the format determined by the Administrator. Quarterly reporting aligns with WIOA and allows earlier detection of reporting issues and seasonal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for reporting (Registration Agency duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency (per §29.25(a) and (b)) is responsible for collecting information about individual apprentices and sponsors and reporting that information to the Department. This clarifies that Registration Agencies must ensure sponsors' reported information is transmitted to OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responsibility ensures SAAs/Registration Agencies are accountable for the completeness and timeliness of data submissions and supports demographic disaggregation for equity monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of collected data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collected under annual sponsor reporting (§29.28(c)) will be made publicly available (e.g., on apprenticeship.gov) and may include raw data in multiple file formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability responds to ACA recommendations to share disaggregated demographic data to promote transparency and enable validation strategies by States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data system interoperability and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet reporting requirements, SAAs must either use Department-provided systems (e.g., RAPIDS) or maintain State systems capable of reporting individual apprentice record-level information in the Administrator-prescribed format and meeting minimum security requirements consistent with FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not mandate RAPIDS but notes its availability and that many States already use it; interoperability mechanisms are encouraged so States can retain local systems while meeting national reporting standards. Using the Department system can defer costs and provide technical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality, disaggregation, and analytic uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collected should be sufficient to disaggregate demographic information, support planning goals, align with WIOA/Perkins planning, rigorously evaluate apprenticeship pathways, capture apprentices' progress (licenses, degrees, credentials), and inform equity indices and data-driven investment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department frames data collection as compulsory for system modernization and equity objectives; better data supports transparency, accountability, and improved program targeting for underserved communities.
